If $A=\begin{bmatrix} -1 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp -1 \\ \end{bmatrix} $, then $$ \det(A - \lambda I) = (\lambda+1)^2 = 0, $$ which implies that there is a single eigenvalue $\lambda=-1$. We find that $$ A-(-1)I = \begin{bmatrix} 0 \amp 0 \\ 0 \amp 0 \\ \end{bmatrix}, $$ which says that every two-dimensional vector $\vvec$ satisfies $(A-(-1)I)\vvec = \zerovec$. Therefore, every vector is an eigenvector and so $E_{-1} = \real^2$. This eigenspace is two-dimensional.

We can see this in another way. The matrix transformation defined by $A$ rotates vectors by $180^\circ$, which says that $A\xvec = -\xvec$ for every vector $\xvec$. In other words, every two-dimensional vector is an eigenvector with associated eigenvalue $\lambda=-1$.
